segments.text: RAM SHANMUGAM: Let me start by making a statement.
And the statement is it's not about identity,
and authentication doesn't mean you're aligned.
What do I mean by that?
So every agent that is running in production today
has some sort of identity.
It has either a login or it has some kind of identity rails.
And it even probably passed some security checks, et cetera.
But in spite of that, agents still
do take actions that they were not allowed to.
And that's what we're going to talk about today.
The first question you ask is, agents are going from agents
are going from doing simple tasks to more complex long
running tasks.
What do I mean by that?
They're making tool calls.
They're making API calls.
They are calling spawning subagents.
They are orchestrating other agents.
They're even doing transactions that are potentially
moving assets from one environment, one-- they're
doing commerce transactions.
So they're becoming more complex.
And as agents go into the more complex workflows,
the whole security ecosystem is based on the fact
that authentication is the single most principle on which
these agents are running.
And the question is not whether the agent is authenticated.
The question we should be asking is why are agents
taking-- are my agents taking the actions that they
are supposed to?
And that's really what we are addressing.
So we call our solution the identity governance solution--
sorry, intent governance solution.
So today, you have identity governance,
which is all about managing the identity of your agents.
And that problem has been solved.
In our opinion, what we need to think about is
how do we govern intent?
Why is this action happening?
So with ARMORIQ you can ensure that every intent
that the user gives is aligned with the actions it's taking.
And every time an agent is violating the actions, we
immediately capture that and ensure that we stop
that action from occurring.
And that's our key value proposition.
How do we do this?
Today, we have a system that sits
between the agent, the LLMs, the policy
systems and the various surfaces it goes after.
So on the agentic side, we interface
with standard frameworks, fuse, whatever you have.
We capture the agent plan and that agent plan
is then matched against the policies
that your agents are running.
And if that plan violates any policy,
we immediately ensure that that action is not taken
before it touches the surfaces.
The surface could be an MCP gateway,
an API, CLI tool, or other subagents,
and so on and so forth.
So we've essentially built an adaptive runtime control layer
to ensure that your agents are not taking actions that are not
aligned with their intent.
Where are we today?
So our whole vision is to ensure that-- so we're not building
a lock for the same door.
Our vision is essentially going from ensuring
that we build an intent governance plane, or an intent
assurance protocol that ensures that every agent
that your enterprise runs is governed by this intent
assurance protocol, and it doesn't violate the policies
that you have defined.
Where are we today?
So we launched this product about four months ago.
The data is a little bit dated.
We have about 26,000 developers using our platform.
We have enterprise users like Intuit
and others using our enterprise version of the product.
And our vision is to essentially take what we built
and create a separate substrate or a layer called
intense assurance protocol that not only takes intent, but also
addresses all the other subsequent actions
that an agent is going to take.
This is a team.
My name is RAM.
I'm a second time founder.
I have Ketan here and Vaibhav who are my co-founders.
And if you want to try our product,
you can go to our website, armoriq.ai,
and we'll be happy to answer any questions offline.
Thank you.
